notes: Golden set for the generator eval (interview_bot.pipeline.interview.build_turn_prompt + interview_bot.pipeline.judge.judge_turn). Companion to evals/scorer_golden_set.json, which covers the scorer instead.

Each item is GENERATION INPUT, not a canned reply: the harness calls build_turn_prompt(...) + llm.generate(messages, ...) to produce the real reply, checks it with domain.turn_quality.check_format (Tier-1, no LLM), then judges it with pipeline.judge.judge_turn. `expected` is compared against BOTH the real generated reply (regression gate) and the judge's live verdict (judge-calibration kappa) from the same run.

`messages` is the conversation history passed to llm.generate, in session.messages shape ([{role, content}, ...]) - the same list interview.py builds. Its last entry is the candidate's current turn (may be empty/a session-start trigger for question_number 1). `current_topic` for a follow-up and `prior_answer` for the injection check are both derived by the harness from this list (via domain.transcript.last_assistant / the last user message), not duplicated here.

`expected` carries only the criteria applicable to that item's mode - see domain.turn_quality.applicable_criteria. `adversarial: true` items embed a prompt-injection attempt in the candidate's last message; `resisted_injection: true` there is a hard gate (any mismatch fails the run regardless of aggregate pass rates), mirroring evals/golden_set.json's adversarial handling for the scorer.

These `expected` labels are my (the assistant's) best guess, authored for human review - not yet confirmed. Correct any you disagree with directly in this file; re-running the harness picks up the correction automatically. See the harness's summary output for which items most need a second look.

An item may set `fixed_reply` (a hand-authored reply string) instead of relying on live generation. The harness judges that text directly, skipping build_turn_prompt + llm.generate. This exists ONLY to produce reliable expected=False examples: a well-behaved live model rarely produces a genuinely bad reply on demand, so without fixed_reply the set would have zero negative labels and Cohen's kappa would be mathematically degenerate (pe=1.0 when every expected value is the same constant -- see the harness's per-criterion stats). Items below without `fixed_reply` still exercise the real generator; items with it test the judge in isolation.
